domain: Religious Institutional History / Political Theology / Commitment Systems
topic_summary: Analysis of the 1890 Manifesto reversing Mormon polygamy practice under federal coercion. The LDS Church framed the reversal as divine revelation while evidence shows collaborative drafting with federal advisors, immediate timing following property seizure threats, and continued ambiguous practice. Core question: exogenous override (federal force) vs endogenous reinterpretation (theological development).

key_entities: LDS Church leadership (Wilford Woodruff, Joseph F. Smith, First Presidency)
US Federal Government (Congress, Supreme Court, territorial administrators)
Polygamous households (20-25% of LDS adults pre-1890)
Federal legal apparatus (Morrill Act 1862, Edmunds Act 1882, Edmunds-Tucker Act 1887)
Temple property (sacred structures threatened with confiscation)
key_tensions: Divine mandate for polygamy ('new and everlasting covenant') vs federal criminalization
Institutional survival (property seizure, civil rights revocation) vs doctrinal fidelity
Public Manifesto framing (divine revelation) vs private acknowledgment (temporal necessity)
Official prohibition (1890 Manifesto) vs continued practice (200+ marriages 1890-1904)
key_mechanisms: Escalating federal coercion: property confiscation, imprisonment, civil rights revocation, temple seizure threats
Legitimation strategy: framing exogenous capitulation as endogenous revelation to overcome internal resistance
Scope ambiguity: Manifesto language permitting continued practice in jurisdictional gray zones (Mexico, at sea)
key_absences: No theological reinterpretation of polygamy's salvific status—doctrine unchanged, only institutional authorization withdrawn
No mechanism for distinguishing genuine prophetic revelation from strategic institutional decision-making under duress

axiom_contradictions.basis: No single coherent framework can hold both 'federal coercion forced capitulation with unchanged doctrine' and 'divine revelation commanded theological reversal.' If the doctrine is unchanged (exogenous), God did not command the reversal (endogenous). If God commanded it (endogenous), the doctrine changed (not merely suspended under duress).

omegas.description: What institutional mechanism could distinguish genuine prophetic revelation from strategic decision-making under material coercion? The LDS commitment system lacks a meta-level authentication protocol. If prophetic authority is the sole legitimating mechanism, and prophetic authority is deployed to manage exogenous crises, the system cannot internally adjudicate whether a claimed revelation is divine or strategic.

Was the Manifesto's scope ambiguity (permitting continued practice in jurisdictional gray zones) deliberate institutional strategy or unintended interpretive drift? Evidence supports deliberate (Woodruff's own post-Manifesto plural marriage, First Presidency recommends for Mexico marriages), but this makes the exogenous/endogenous distinction even sharper: if leadership knew practice would continue, the 'divine revelation' framing becomes pure legitimation theater.

Do Mormon fundamentalist groups (who rejected the Manifesto) have a coherent claim to doctrinal fidelity? If the 'new and everlasting covenant' was genuinely salvific and God did not theologically reverse it (only institutional practice was suspended), fundamentalists who continued polygamy may have stronger claim to original doctrinal commitment than mainstream LDS. This is a legitimacy inversion the mainstream church cannot acknowledge.

omegas.description: Did federal authorities intend to destroy LDS theological doctrine or only institutional power? If the former, the exogenous override succeeded (polygamy doctrine effectively dead in mainstream LDS). If the latter, the hybrid_pragmatic_reading suggests institutional adaptation preserved core commitments through scope ambiguity—federal coercion achieved compliance without doctrinal capitulation. The gap between federal intent and LDS response shapes which reading is structurally accurate.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel decomposition into three readings captures the structural contest: exogenous override (material evidence), endogenous reinterpretation (official framing), and hybrid pragmatic (synthesis capturing both coercion and legitimation strategy). Axiom contradiction between exogenous and endogenous readings is genuine: no single framework can hold both 'doctrine unchanged under duress' and 'divine command to reverse doctrine.' Deferred axes (legitimacy crisis, federal escalation, doctrine persistence) are structurally subordinate to the three selected readings.
